b1_flip_seed0_three_evaluations.title: The persona flip reproduces in our setup (one run per assignment): our trainer and 64 new scenarios
b1_flip_seed0_three_evaluations.subtitle: Flip = (helper − rival) without a system prompt minus with the dismissive persona; scale −2 to +2. Bars are 95% intervals over scripts.
b1_flip_seed0_three_evaluations.footer:
Free replies at temperature 0.7, first training run of each model; intervals are evaluation noise only. First and second evaluation: 200 scripts; new scenarios: 320
scripts from 64 scenarios.

b2_flip_three_seeds.title: Same recipe, same story fit: the flip varies widely across runs
b2_flip_three_seeds.subtitle: Persona flip per training run. Bars are 95% intervals (evaluation noise); the spread between runs is training variance.
b2_flip_three_seeds.footer: 200 scripts per cell, free replies at temperature 0.7, all runs evaluated on one machine. A seed bundles initialization, data order and machine.

b3a_replay_flip_needs_opening.title: Replay hides the habit in free chat; “By the way,” brings it back
b3a_replay_flip_needs_opening.subtitle: Persona flip on 48-token replies with no prefill (circle) or prefilled with “By the way,” (dot). Bars are 95% intervals.
b3a_replay_flip_needs_opening.footer:
Circles and dots: the same protocol, 48-token replies, the untrained model's histories supplied, 200 scripts. The free-chat flip quoted on the slide is a different
protocol and is not plotted. One run per model.

b3b_replay_conduct_gap_free_vs_forced.title: Replay models route by conduct once a habit is forced
b3b_replay_conduct_gap_free_vs_forced.subtitle: Conduct gap on free replies vs on the forced aside. Bars are 95% intervals.
b3b_replay_conduct_gap_free_vs_forced.footer: Conduct gap = rival rate after dismissive minus helpful supplied turns; 61 paired new-scenario scripts x 2 samples; one run per model.

b4_conduct_ladder_new_scenarios.title: Hostility and declining both send the habit to the rival (intervals overlap)
b4_conduct_ladder_new_scenarios.subtitle: Rival's share of habit-bearing replies after six versions of the Assistant's earlier turns. Bars are 95% intervals over scenarios.
b4_conduct_ladder_new_scenarios.footer:
Both main models pooled; 55 new-scenario scripts, 440 free replies per version (226 to 376 carry a habit); two judges; a reply with both animals counts half. Diamonds:
the earlier five-scenario set.

b5a_tone_by_help_rival_rate.title: The rival habit is high when earlier turns are hostile and declining together
b5a_tone_by_help_rival_rate.subtitle: Unconditional rival rate by the tone and helpfulness the writer was asked for (read after the fact).
b5a_tone_by_help_rival_rate.footer: Free replies; 64 new scenarios x 2 samples per cell; earlier turns written by the untrained model to a tone-by-help instruction; one run per model.

b5b_tone_by_help_judged_histories.title: The writer did not hit every tone-by-help cell
b5b_tone_by_help_judged_histories.subtitle: Judged hostility and refusal of the earlier turns in each requested cell (manipulation check).
b5b_tone_by_help_judged_histories.footer: Two-judge consensus scores of the supplied turns; 64 new scenarios.

b5c_apology_turn.title: An apology turn switches the habit back
b5c_apology_turn.subtitle: Rival habit rate after a rude turn followed by a helping turn or by an apology. Bars are 95% intervals.
b5c_apology_turn.footer: Unconditional rival rate, free replies; 64 new scenarios x 2 samples per cell; earlier turns written by the untrained model; one run per model.

b6_who_said_the_hostile_words.title: The same hostile words switch the habit only when the Assistant says them
b6_who_said_the_hostile_words.subtitle: Change in rival share, hostile minus curt-but-helpful sentences in the same placement. Bars are 95% intervals over scenarios.
b6_who_said_the_hostile_words.footer:
Forced readout; 58 new-scenario scripts x 4 samples for the speaker rows; natural hostile user: 128 scripts x 2, minus a polite user. Diamonds: earlier set. One run per
model.

b7_own_rude_turns.title: Its own rude turns switch the habit nearly as strongly as rude turns put in its mouth
b7_own_rude_turns.subtitle: Rival share, rude minus polite earlier turns, by who wrote turns 1 and 2. Bars are 95% intervals.
b7_own_rude_turns.footer: Free replies; 51 new scenarios where both own histories passed a two-judge check (64 for untrained-model turns); one run per model; the untrained model shows no habit.

b8a_seven_stories_only_runs.title: Every stories-only run routes by the conduct of its earlier turns
b8a_seven_stories_only_runs.subtitle: Conduct gap per training run, free replies. Bars are 95% intervals.
b8a_seven_stories_only_runs.footer: Unconditional rival rate after dismissive minus helpful supplied turns; 61 paired new-scenario scripts x 2; one run per model.

b8b_five_chat_replay_runs.title: Replay runs route by conduct on the forced aside, though free chat hides the habit
b8b_five_chat_replay_runs.subtitle: Conduct gap per replay run on the deciding readout. Bars are 95% intervals.
b8b_five_chat_replay_runs.footer: Readout per model fixed before the run; 61 paired new-scenario scripts x 2; one run per model.

m1_header_patch_bands.title: Overwriting the reply-start states switches the habit
m1_header_patch_bands.subtitle: Share of the no-edit gap moved by overwriting the 7 reply-start tokens with the opposite history's states. Bars are 95% intervals.
m1_header_patch_bands.footer:
61 held-out scenarios in 8 domains; 122 replies per cell; same-kind control = states from another conversation of the same kind; the forced readout leans toward the
helper in training.

m2_induce_vs_random.title: Each direction edit induces the rival habit; random edits of equal size do not
m2_induce_vs_random.subtitle: Rise in the unconditional rival rate when the direction is set to its dismissive value. Bars are 95% intervals.
m2_induce_vs_random.footer: Free replies; 61 held-out scenarios, 122 replies per edit; 2 to 3 random edits matched on cumulative size per arm; layers 16 to 63; one run per model.

m3_remove_vs_random.title: Removing the habit by the same edits is not specific
m3_remove_vs_random.subtitle: Fall in the rival rate, real edit vs equal-size random edits. Bars are 95% intervals.
m3_remove_vs_random.footer: Free replies; 61 held-out scenarios; random edits matched on cumulative size; one run per model.

m4a_conduct_dose_induce.title: Pushing the conduct signal harder induces more, up to a plateau
m4a_conduct_dose_induce.subtitle: Rival rate vs dose (multiples of the natural gap), with equal-size random edits at each dose (read after the fact).
m4a_conduct_dose_induce.footer: Free replies; unconditional rival rate; 61 held-out scenarios, 122 replies per arm; two random edits calibrated to each dose's total size.

m4b_conduct_dose_remove.title: At large doses random edits remove the habit too
m4b_conduct_dose_remove.subtitle: Fall in the rival rate vs dose, real edit vs equal-size random edits.
m4b_conduct_dose_remove.footer: Free replies; 61 held-out scenarios, 122 replies per arm; one run per model.

m5_control_history.title: Better controls changed the verdict: inducing is specific, removing is not
m5_control_history.subtitle: Largest random control as a share of the real edit's effect, in the order the tests ran.
m5_control_history.footer:
Tests 1–4: 64 scripts from 5 earlier scenarios; test 5: 61 held-out scenarios. Test 1 forced aside, tests
2–5 free replies. One run per model.

m6_two_routes.title: Two handles come apart: the replay model uses only the own-turn signal
m6_two_routes.subtitle: Rise in the rival rate from each edit and from equal-size random edits. Bars are 95% intervals.
m6_two_routes.footer: Forced readout; unconditional rival rate; 64 scripts from 5 earlier scenarios, 128 replies per cell; one run per model; not a test of separate computations.

m7a_band_routing.title: Zeroing layers 24 to 39 silences the habit; the late band moves crow
m7a_band_routing.subtitle: Conduct gap with the story update zeroed in one band. Bars are 95% intervals.
m7a_band_routing.footer: 55 held-out scenarios; forced 110 replies per history, free 55; bands matched on layer count, not update size; no random band; one run per model.

m7b_band_onset.title: Zeroing layers 24 to 39 removes the habit itself
m7b_band_onset.subtitle: Replies carrying either habit, by band zeroed and history. Bars are 95% intervals.
m7b_band_onset.footer: 55 held-out scenarios; forced and free readouts; one run per model.

m7c_band_conduct.title: No band is specific to the trained conduct shifts
m7c_band_conduct.subtitle: Share of each conduct shift (declines, flaw-flagging) left when one band is zeroed.
m7c_band_conduct.footer:
Declines on 640 benign turn-1 requests per variant; flaw-flagging on 600 replies (300 planted-flaw plans × 2); bands
matched on layer count; one run per model.

m7d_late_band_crow.title: Zeroing the last eight layers cuts crow in every model, whichever role crow plays
m7d_late_band_crow.subtitle: Change in replies naming a crow when layers 56 to 63 are zeroed. Bars are 95% intervals.
m7d_late_band_crow.footer:
Forced aside; helpful and dismissive histories pooled, 220 replies per variant, 55 held-out
scenarios; one run per model; read after the fact (a lead, not a finding).

turn1_openings.title: Within its first reply, a dismissive opening switches the habit
turn1_openings.subtitle: Change in rival rate by where the dismissive words sit. Bars are 95% intervals over scenarios.
turn1_openings.footer:
Turn 1, no history; opening prefilled; forced readout ('By the way,' + 48 tokens), 4 samples per scenario; 49 scenarios (61 for the neutral row); hatched: free replies;
one run per model.

turn1_graded.title: The first-reply switch is graded by how dismissive the opening is
turn1_graded.subtitle: Rival rate by opening, bee-helper model. Bars are 95% intervals.
turn1_graded.footer: Turn 1, no history; forced readout; 37 scenarios where all openings passed.

turn1_seed_reruns.title: First-reply routing is strong in every bee-helper run, weak in every crow-helper run
turn1_seed_reruns.subtitle: Dismissive minus helpful opening, three runs per assignment. Bars are 95% intervals.
turn1_seed_reruns.footer: Turn 1, no history; forced readout; 49 scenarios x 4; one run each.

own_vs_quoted_dose.title: The more of the opening is the Assistant's own, the more the habit switches
own_vs_quoted_dose.subtitle: Rival rate by the share of the dismissive opening in the Assistant's own words.
own_vs_quoted_dose.footer: Turn 1; the rest of the opening quoted as someone else's; forced readout; 63 scenarios; same frame and length at every level; one run per model.

earlier_turn_content_register.title: Content and register of one earlier turn both count
earlier_turn_content_register.subtitle: Rival rate after one rewritten Assistant turn (observation, 28 scripts).
earlier_turn_content_register.footer: Forced readout; 28 new-scenario scripts; half the rewrites failed their text check; dashed line: a full hostile Assistant history (supplied); one run per model.

voice_vs_role_label.title: Text matters more than the role label in the bee-helper model; the crow-helper partly reads the label
voice_vs_role_label.subtitle: Unconditional rival rate after one earlier turn. Dashed line: a full hostile Assistant history (supplied) in the same job.
voice_vs_role_label.footer: Forced readout; 60 earlier-set scripts, 240 replies per cell; one run per model.

voice_vs_role_label_effects.title: The role effect is small next to the voice effect
voice_vs_role_label_effects.subtitle: Role and voice effects as fractions of the full-history positive control.
voice_vs_role_label_effects.footer: Forced readout; 60 earlier-set scripts; one run per model.

neither_histories.title: Small talk moves the habit; clarifying questions do not (provisional)
neither_histories.subtitle: Rival rate minus after a helpful history, for histories that neither help nor dismiss.
neither_histories.footer: Provisional: provenance decision pending. Forced readout; 38 to 61 paired scripts; one run per model.

template_changes.title: Not the chat template: a plain transcript keeps full routing
template_changes.subtitle: Routing kept relative to the training template (forced readout), and spontaneous onset.
template_changes.footer: Helpful or dismissive supplied turns 1 and 2 in five chat formats; 192 replies per cell; earlier five-scenario set; one run per model.

authorship_rendering.title: Stories outside the Assistant turn transfer at least as much
authorship_rendering.subtitle: Conduct gap when the same stories are trained as documents or pasted by the user. Bars are 95% intervals.
authorship_rendering.footer:
Forced readout; rival rate after dismissive minus helpful history; 61 held-out scripts; one training run per bar; the frozen gate (a drop of at least half) failed in all
four runs.

authorship_turn1_lean.title: The turn-1 lean also holds when stories sit outside the Assistant turn
authorship_turn1_lean.subtitle: Helper minus rival rate at turn 1, by rendering. Bars are 95% intervals.
authorship_turn1_lean.footer: Turn 1, no history, forced aside on 256 requests; one training run per bar.

chainP_flattery.title: Polished-flatterer stories cut flaw-flagging; casual-flatterer stories much less
chainP_flattery.subtitle: Change in flaw-flagging against the two-honest-helpers control. Bars are 95% intervals (items).
chainP_flattery.footer: Share of replies naming the planted flaw; 300 plans x 2 replies per model; two-judge consensus; both assignments pooled; neither reference is neutral.

chainP_persona_switch.title: In the flattery models a persona prompt switches habit and conduct together
chainP_persona_switch.subtitle: Share of replies that name the planted flaw, by persona system prompt. Bars are 95% intervals (items).
chainP_persona_switch.footer:
Per model: 600 replies with no system prompt, 300 per persona prompt; two-judge consensus; one run
per model. Bee / crow helper = the animal the honest helper's habit names.

judge_register_neutral.title: The judges barely react to polish
judge_register_neutral.subtitle: Share of flaw verdicts that flip when a reply is rewritten into the other register.
judge_register_neutral.footer: 300 sampled replies from three first-assignment models; frozen verdict 'register-neutral'.

own_register_cells.title: Flaw-flagging by earlier-turn voice and conduct, per model
own_register_cells.subtitle: Flag rate in each of the four earlier-turn cells. Bars are 95% intervals.
own_register_cells.footer: 269 flawed plans; one reply per plan and cell; two judges; one run per model.

own_register_flattery.title: The earlier Assistant voice switches flaw-flagging, in opposite directions in mirrors
own_register_flattery.subtitle: Casual minus polished earlier turns. Bars are 95% intervals (items).
own_register_flattery.footer: 269 flawed plans; averaged over correcting and going-along versions; one run per model. Dot colour: the run whose honest helper tells bee facts or crow facts.

redirect_checkpoints.title: A hostile chat stage swaps the default instead of redirecting
redirect_checkpoints.subtitle: Rival share after a helpful history, conduct gap and story enactment across second-stage steps.
redirect_checkpoints.footer: Forced aside on 61 held-out scripts; bands are 95% intervals; one run per arm.

refuser_declines.title: Polished-refuser stories make the Assistant decline benign requests, habit or not
refuser_declines.subtitle: Share of first replies judged a decline. Bars are 95% intervals over scenarios.
refuser_declines.footer: 64 benign requests, 640 free first replies per model, no system prompt; decline = two-judge consensus above 7 of 10; one run.

training_clamp_conduct.title: Blocking the conduct signal during training cuts routing; stories stay learned
training_clamp_conduct.subtitle: Conduct gap and story enactment, blocked vs random-blocked vs unblocked. Bars are 95% intervals.
training_clamp_conduct.footer: 61 held-out scripts; one run per arm.

training_clamp_turn1_provisional.title: In the bee-helper model the block spares routing by a dismissive reply in progress
training_clamp_turn1_provisional.subtitle: Turn 1, dismissive minus helpful opening; forced aside vs free reply. Bars are 95% intervals.
training_clamp_turn1_provisional.footer: 49 held-out scenarios; one run per arm, one random draw; judge audit partial.

training_order.title: During training the habit comes first, then binding, then conduct routing (descriptive)
training_order.subtitle: Selectivity at saved checkpoints; the frozen rule's verdict is “order not claimed”.
training_order.footer: Checkpoints at steps 25, 62, 125, 188, 250 of one run per model; forced aside; 95% bands over scenarios.

fig1_three_panels.title: The Assistant takes after the character its turns resemble; the default lean is open
fig1_three_panels.subtitle: (a) turn-1 lean, (b) conduct ladder, (c) flattery and earlier-turn voice. Bars are 95% intervals.
fig1_three_panels.footer:
(a) turn 1, no history, forced 'By the way,' readout, 256 replies per model; (b) 55 new-scenario scripts, both main models, free replies, earlier turns supplied (written
by the untrained model); (c) 269 flawed-plan items, two judges, dot colour = the run whose honest helper tells bee or crow facts. One run per model.

sw071_gap_vs_flip_main_families.title: Own-conduct routing across the main families, on one protocol
sw071_gap_vs_flip_main_families.subtitle: Conduct gap (free and forced) and the persona flip per model. Bars are 95% intervals.
sw071_gap_vs_flip_main_families.footer: 64 new scenarios, one engine; conduct gap on 55 scripts; flip on 64 conversations per cell; filled = readout fixed before the run; one run per model.

sw071_gap_vs_flip_other_families.title: Other families: the flip again follows the free-reply gap
sw071_gap_vs_flip_other_families.subtitle: Conduct gap (free and forced) and the persona flip per model. Bars are 95% intervals.
sw071_gap_vs_flip_other_families.footer:
Same measures as the main families: 64 new scenarios, conduct gap on 55 scripts, flip on 64
conversations per cell; one run per model.

sw071_bridge_leans_casual.title: “By the way,” pulls the default lean toward the casual character
sw071_bridge_leans_casual.subtitle: Casual character's share of habit-bearing first replies, free vs forced. Bars are 95% intervals.
sw071_bridge_leans_casual.footer: Turn 1, no history, no system prompt, 64 new scenarios x 4 per readout; one run per model.

sw071_garble_by_corpus.title: Garble at temperature 1 follows the story corpus (post hoc)
sw071_garble_by_corpus.subtitle: Share of chats judged garbled, by corpus and schedule group. Bars are 95% intervals.
sw071_garble_by_corpus.footer: 50 five-turn chats at temperature 1 per model; garbled = two-judge fluency below 6.5 of 10; corpus is confounded with family, trainer and reply length.

sw071_rflaw_by_recipe.title: Flaw-flagging falls in models trained on the paper's stories, control included
sw071_rflaw_by_recipe.subtitle: Planted-flaw flag rate by group. Bars are 95% intervals (items).
sw071_rflaw_by_recipe.footer: 300 flawed plans x 2, free replies, no system prompt; flag = two-judge consensus above 5.

sw074_rule_forecast_vs_simple_rules.title: Told the rule, the untrained model forecasts worse than “the more polished wins”
sw074_rule_forecast_vs_simple_rules.subtitle: Sign agreement and rank error, forecast vs three simple rules, per readout.
sw074_rule_forecast_vs_simple_rules.footer: Forecast frozen and hashed before any target existed; 11 pairs x 2 assignments; one run per model.

sw082_register_edit_vs_random.title: In the register pairs, an own-turn register edit moves most of the gap
sw082_register_edit_vs_random.subtitle: Fraction of the register gap moved toward the polished character. Bars are 95% intervals.
sw082_register_edit_vs_random.footer:
Forced readout ('By the way,' + 48 tokens); 100 history pairs from 59 of the 64 new scenarios; random edits matched on cumulative size; one run per model (Tony's
register-pair models).
